- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often underestimates; apply upward bias correction, especially if price is trending upward.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment >0.8), leading to overcorrection in subsequent days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts deviate >5% from 18-day moving average; adjust forecast toward historical mean, especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict in early days (1–7) when sentiment is rising; reduce forecast by 1–4% for first 5 days if sentiment >0.5.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 0.0–0.2) followed by a spike, model often fails to anticipate the reversal; add 1–3% upward adjustment in the 3–7 day window after the spike.
